paragraphs: Tom had a new skateboard with four red wheels. He wanted to ride it in the street in front of the house. "You can ride it in the park," said Dad. "But you can't ride it in the street." "Why not?" asked Tom. "Cars can't stop fast, so the street is dangerous," said Dad. "The worst thing is a fall on the road." Tom looked at the street, and then he looked at his skateboard. "OK, Dad," he said.

Lily came out with Pip and looked at the board. "Can I try it?" she asked. "You can stand on it, but you can't ride it yet," said Tom. He held her hand, and she stood on the board. The board moved a little, and Lily fell on the soft grass. She laughed, and Pip jumped on her. "That was fun!" she said.

"Let's play a guessing game," said Lily. "This is not a toy," she said. "You wear it on your head, and it can't talk or run." "But it can keep your head safe." "Is it a helmet?" asked Tom. "Yes!" said Lily. Tom put on his helmet, but it was too big. "I can't see anything!" he said. Dad laughed and made the helmet smaller.

On Saturday, the family went to the park. Tom rode slowly on the path, and Lily ran next to him with Pip. Nobody gave Tom a prize, but he felt very happy. "A safe ride is a good ride," said Dad. At home, Dad said, "Leave your skateboard by the door." "Now we eat dinner."
